summary: Málaga's Sustainable Mobility ordinance has applied since 30 November 2024 and defines a Zona de Bajas Emisiones that the city puts at 437 hectares, controlled by licence-plate recognition, with fines for unlabelled vehicles not domiciled in the city from 30 November 2025; in June 2026 the Andalusian High Court annulled the domicile-based access rules, a ruling reported as not final and open to cassation appeal. On-street SARE parking has cost 1 euro per hour under a new fiscal ordinance since 1 January 2026, and SMASSA, the municipal car park company, has been 100% publicly owned since 30 December 2024, with a merger with the EMT bus company planned. The city's central municipal car park network offers 5,066 spaces (Feria 2026 plan), while new capacity is at the planning stage, including a 135-space surface car park near Baños del Carmen and park-and-ride studies for Martín Carpena and the Totalán stream. Demand pressures include 26.76 million airport passengers in 2025 and more than 50 million EMT bus trips in 2024.

items.text: Málaga's new Sustainable Mobility ordinance, which regulates the Zona de Bajas Emisiones (ZBE), pedestrian-priority zones and the SARE regulated on-street parking, was published in the BOP on 29 November 2024 and entered into force on 30 November 2024. The city describes a 437-hectare ZBE controlled with licence-plate recognition linked to DGT and municipal register data. Access was phased: in year one vehicles with label CERO/ECO/C, label B and vehicles with no label could all circulate; in year two unlabelled vehicles had to be domiciled in Málaga; from year three label B vehicles also have to be domiciled in Málaga.
items.source_title: Publicada en el BOP la nueva ordenanza de Movilidad Sostenible de la ciudad de Málaga

items.text: On 27 November 2025 the city announced that the second year of the Sustainable Mobility ordinance would start on Sunday 30 November 2025, restricting access to the ZBE for cars and motorbikes without an environmental label that were not domiciled in Málaga. Vehicles labelled CERO, ECO, C and B could still circulate during the second year; from the third year (30 November 2026) the limit would extend to label B vehicles not domiciled in Málaga.
items.source_title: El 30 de noviembre comienza el segundo año de vigencia de la ordenanza de Movilidad Sostenible

items.text: A March 2026 study by the University of Málaga's Cátedra de Gestión del Transporte, promoted by the city's Mobility Area, states that the ZBE entered into force on 30 November 2024, that the first year was a trial and information period and that the sanctioning phase began on 30 November 2025. It describes control by licence-plate recognition systems connected to DGT and municipal register databases, so drivers do not need to display the environmental label.
items.source_title: Opinión ciudadana sobre la ZBE de Málaga: conocimiento y valoración

items.text: On 10 June 2026 El Español reported that the Andalusian High Court (TSJA) had annulled the Málaga ZBE access regulation because it established discriminatory treatment between vehicles domiciled in the capital and those from other municipalities. The report says the city's legal services would study the ruling without ruling out a cassation appeal, and that the ruling was not final.
items.source_title: Varapalo judicial para la Zona de Bajas Emisiones de Málaga

items.text: For Semana Santa 2026 the city's mobility plan states that the Centro Histórico access-control system on the Carretería-Álamos axis and calle Cisneros would be temporarily disabled from Friday 27 March to Monday 6 April 2026. Processions cut traffic on Boquete del Muelle, Paseo del Parque, Plaza de la Marina, Alameda Principal and calle Córdoba, and SARE regulation was suppressed on several streets on specified days (for example Avenida Manuel Agustín Heredia on 30-31 March and 1 and 4 April).

For Semana Santa 2025 (12-20 April) the city advised against private vehicle use in the centre and announced 400,000 additional EMT seats. The municipal car parks of Camas, Tejón y Rodríguez and Plaza de la Marina would close once Local Police traffic cuts were made, while Alcazaba, Cervantes and Andalucía would have restrictions; Cervantes, Andalucía, San Juan de la Cruz and Salitre were stated to remain open.
items.source_title: El Ayuntamiento pone en marcha el plan especial de movilidad con motivo de la Semana Santa 2025

items.text: The Feria de Málaga 2026 mobility plan (15-22 August) says the municipal car park network in the centre and surroundings offers 5,066 spaces (Plaza la Marina, San Juan de la Cruz, Tejón y Rodríguez, Alcazaba, Camas, Andalucía, Cervantes and Salitre). Cervantes, Alcazaba, Camas, Tejón y Rodríguez, Plaza la Marina, Andalucía, Salitre, San Juan de la Cruz, Carlos Haya, Cruz de Humilladero, Pío Baroja and El Palo were to stay open 24 hours. The plan lists 3,185 car spaces at the Real (Cortijo de Torres) and says the Centro Histórico access-control system would follow the Bando de Feria.

The new fiscal ordinance no. 22 on the regulated on-street parking tax (SARE) took effect on 1 January 2026 (approved by the Pleno on 30 January 2025, published in the BOP on 31 December 2025). The general rate is 1.00 euro per hour, with a minimum of 0.50 euro per 30 minutes and a maximum of 2.50 euros per 150 minutes. Residents pay 0.20 euro per 24 hours or 1.00 euro per 168 hours. If the paid time is exceeded, the charge is 5.00 euros, and parking without a ticket costs 9.00 euros, in both cases if regularised voluntarily within three days. SMASSA assists the municipal tax administration in managing, inspecting and collecting the tax.
items.source_title: Ordenanza Fiscal nº 22 reguladora de la tasa por el estacionamiento regulado de vehículos en las vías públicas de la ciudad de Málaga

items.text: SMASSA became a 100% publicly owned company on 30 December 2024, when the city completed buying the 49% of shares held by Unicaja and Empark. On 8 April 2025 the SMASSA board was to approve new statutes (name changed to Sociedad Municipal de Aparcamientos y Servicios S.A.M.), as part of a merger procedure with the EMT bus company that began on 30 January 2025 so that one company manages the city's mobility.
items.source_title: El consejo de Smassa dará luz verde a la aprobación de los nuevos estatutos de la sociedad

items.text: A city press release of 4 October 2023 states that since 2000 SMASSA has promoted three parking plans with 53 car parks built in the city's neighbourhoods, totalling more than 14,140 resident spaces. SMASSA has built 11 mixed (resident and rotation) car parks, including San Juan de la Cruz, Tejón y Rodríguez, Carlos de Haya, Avenida de Andalucía, El Palo, Cervantes, Salitre and Pío Baroja, plus La Marina as rotation-only. The release also announced a study of a new underground car park near Baños del Carmen in Pedregalejo.
items.source_title: El Ayuntamiento inicia el estudio de viabilidad de un nuevo aparcamiento en el distrito Este

items.text: On 1 March 2024 the city completed the commissioning of the Pío Baroja car park in Echeverría del Palo: an underground car park costing more than 11 million euros with 146 owned spaces and 276 rotation spaces (operational since July 2023). Rotation tariffs quoted (VAT not included) were 0.0370 euro per minute for minutes 0-30, 0.0050 euro per minute for minutes 61-720 and 0.0001 euro per minute for minutes 721-1,440. The owned spaces were priced at 23,140.50 euros each (VAT not included).
items.source_title: El Ayuntamiento completa la entrada en servicio del aparcamiento en rotación y para residentes Pío Baroja en Echeverría del Palo

items.text: On 16 June 2026 the city presented the construction project for a new surface rotation car park in the Baños del Carmen area (Málaga Este), to be managed by SMASSA: 135 rotation spaces on 3,641 m2, 4 of them for reduced-mobility users and 4 with electric-vehicle charging points (expandable), 89 new trees and links to EMT lines L3, L8, L11, L33 and L34. The municipal investment is about 2 million euros plus 3.6 million euros spent by Urbanismo to obtain the land.
items.source_title: El Ayuntamiento impulsa un nuevo aparcamiento en rotación en el distrito Este con 135 plazas y conectado con las líneas de la EMT

items.text: On 17 October 2025 the city, through SMASSA, announced the award to Desarrollo Organización y Movilidad S.A. of a study of demand, access and layout alternatives for a park-and-ride (aparcamiento disuasorio) near the MA-24 and the Totalán stream, for 44,570.68 euros (VAT included) and a four-month execution period. The release says the study of the park-and-ride next to the Martín Carpena Sports Palace was already done and that its preliminary design (anteproyecto) was being drafted.
items.source_title: El Ayuntamiento adjudica el estudio de la demanda para el impulso del aparcamiento disuasorio junto al arroyo de Totalán

items.text: An undated city mobility summary sheet (ficha) of a study commissioned by Promálaga and the city's Mobility Area proposes, as preliminary ideas to be detailed in future projects, a park-and-ride of 467 new spaces (16 for electric vehicles and 10 for reduced-mobility users) in a two-level solution at the Martín Carpena Sports Palace, in addition to the 750 existing spaces associated with the palace. It estimates a budget of 20-23 million euros for the car park plus 6-14 million euros for accesses (VAT included), says about 40-45% of the future demand would arise from other measures discouraging private vehicle use, with the ZBE being relevant, and in principle does not suggest charging a tariff.
items.source_title: Asistencia técnica para la elaboración de un estudio de demanda, accesos y alternativas para aparcamiento disuasorio en el entorno del Palacio de Deportes Martín Carpena (Málaga)

items.text: On 24 August 2026 El Español reported that a provisional 750-space paid car park was due to open at 06:00 the following day (Tuesday 25 August) at the Hospital Civil while the new Hospital Virgen de la Esperanza is built: 163 spaces reserved and discounted for professionals and 587 for general use. The public rate was given as 1.36 euros per hour (known since May 2026; the article's standfirst says 1.63, apparently a typo) and the professional rate as 0.61 euro per hour; staff protested that they previously paid 0.80 euro a day.
items.source_title: Abren el parking de pago de 750 plazas en el Hospital Civil de Málaga: 163 son para profesionales

items.text: On 11 August 2026 the Junta de Gobierno Local gave approval to the detail study (stage described as initial approval, with public consultation and a binding Civil Aviation report still to follow) allowing the Palacio de Ferias y Congresos (Fycma) to be extended by more than 37,000 m2 on an adjacent plot currently used for parking; the proposal includes two underground parking floors of about 2,000 spaces to replace the affected spaces and serve new demand. The same release reports approval of an action project by the University of Málaga for a 'green' long-stay vehicle car park (about 1,365 spaces estimated) on the Finca La Máquina Grande, about 200 metres from the airport runway threshold, with public consultation still to open.
items.source_title: El Ayuntamiento avanza en la tramitación urbanística para la ampliación del Palacio de Ferias y Congresos de Málaga

items.text: Aena reported on 13 January 2026 that Málaga-Costa del Sol Airport closed 2025 with 26,760,549 passengers (+7.4% on 2024) and 186,990 flights, its busiest year on record.
items.source_title: El Aeropuerto de Málaga-Costa del Sol cierra un año histórico con más de 26,7 millones de pasajeros y cerca de 187.000 operaciones
